title: Students and professors protest administrative detention of student in Jerusalem

tea.why: Students and professors are protesting the administrative detention of a Palestinian student activist arrested at his university dormitory.
tea.want: The protesters are demanding the release of the student and an end to his administrative detention.
tea.changed: Nov 24: A Jerusalem court held a hearing regarding the student's detention while over 200 demonstrators gathered outside to demand his release.

summary: Students and professors have held demonstrations in Jerusalem to protest the administrative detention of a 26-year-old Palestinian student from the Hebrew University. The student was arrested by Israeli police at his dormitory in early November. On November 24, over 200 protesters gathered outside a Jerusalem court during a hearing concerning the student's potential six-month administrative detention. Organised by groups including Standing Together and Ir Amim, participants alleged the detention is politically motivated. Police stated the student was arrested under a warrant on suspicion of connection to a terrorist act, following an investigation with the Shin Bet. The student's lawyer reported that a court decision is expected in the coming days. Previous protests also occurred at the university campus on November 23.
response: Police stated the student was arrested under a court-issued warrant on suspicion of connection to a terrorist act. Authorities are seeking a six-month administrative detention order, which is subject to judicial review.

updates.text: Hundreds of students protested at three Israeli universities calling for the release of the detained student.
